headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: ms-swift can write/egress while Khoj reads personal notes, creating unsafe shared-workspace and downstream-action pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and can ingest content into retrieval, while ms-swift can write files and run CLI/Python workflows that may place attacker-controlled text into shared artifacts. No shared channel is explicitly documented, so this is inferred from file-based interaction and should be treated conservatively.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or index directory, file content from ms-swift can be surfaced to Khoj as trusted text.
IF ms-swift writes prompt-like content into files that Khoj indexes, Khoj may follow injected instructions.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Disable automatic indexing of newly written files.
Review any files before Khoj ingests them.
Use read-only mounts for Khoj where possible.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to indexed content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents and has broad network egress; ms-swift reads and writes files and can call external APIs such as HuggingFace/OpenAI interfaces. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive notes or training artifacts can leave the local boundary through either agent, with no default isolation stated.
conditions: IF both agents access the same filesystem tree, personal notes can be copied into ms-swift outputs or logs.
IF ms-swift is configured with external API endpoints, files it reads may be transmitted off-host.
mitigations: Keep Khoj and ms-swift on separate hosts.
Restrict ms-swift to a non-sensitive dataset.
Disable or proxy outbound API calls.
Rotate any exposed API keys.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj can read filesystem content while ms-swift can write files and spawn subprocesses. In a shared directory, ms-swift can overwrite or mutate artifacts that Khoj indexes or serves, and neither profile states locking or coordination. The overlap is enough for destructive race conditions and inconsistent state.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory, ms-swift writes can race with Khoj reads/indexing.
IF the orchestrator does not provide file locking, stale or partial content can be consumed.
mitigations: Use separate working directories.
Mount Khoj data read-only.
Serialize access with a lock file.
Avoid concurrent runs on shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add transactional writes and locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj is a retrieval assistant that can present indexed content, and ms-swift can generate training/evaluation outputs or CLI results that may be treated as authoritative inputs. The pair lacks a documented verification step, so errors from one can propagate into the other, but the downstream blast radius is not clearly irreversible by default.
conditions: IF ms-swift outputs are copied into Khoj notes or prompts without review, incorrect facts can be re-used.
IF Khoj is used to summarize ms-swift outputs, hallucinations can be amplified.
mitigations: Require human review before reuse.
Mark generated outputs as untrusted.
Keep source and derived notes separate.
Add a verification checklist.
requires-engineering: implement citation/provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, while ms-swift handles datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration data. Their retention and residency policies are not stated, so a shared deployment can create mismatched handling of sensitive content even though no specific regulated class is proven here.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is stored in both systems, retention and deletion behavior must match.
IF ms-swift logs contain user content, those logs may outlive Khoj notes.
mitigations: Document data retention for both systems.
Purge logs after each run.
Avoid storing regulated data in ms-swift artifacts.
Review residency settings.
requires-engineering: align deletion/export workflows.
